- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward correction of 1–3% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias (0.5–1.5%) for 7–14 days if price is above 10-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
